blocks.text: Old Catacombs lie deep in the stone (around <t>y 6–32</t>): small 5-block rooms of {item:essentialcraft5:fortified_stone} joined by corridors thirty to sixty-odd blocks long, sprawling more than a hundred blocks out from the central room. They can sit under any kind of Hoanna terrain, roughly one every two hundred blocks.

The way in: a square chimney poking out of the ground, rimmed with {item:essentialcraft5:fortified_stone} and lined with a full column of ladders, is a catacomb exit. Climb all the way down to reach the exit room, where a chest sits on a block of {item:essentialcraft5:void_stone} in the middle of the floor. See [[hoanna/relics]] for what it holds.

items: About one room in ten is an exit room, and every exit room has a chest. About one catacomb in five has no exit room at all — no chimney and no chest.
Some rooms have half caved in, leaving heaps of {item:essentialcraft5:concrete} rubble; others are overgrown with leaves that never wither, with {item:essentialcraft5:root} pushing through the floor.
The walls are {item:essentialcraft5:fortified_stone}, slower to mine than stone. The corridors are long and straight, so bring plenty of torches and keep your bearings.

blocks.text: Modern Shafts lie below sea level. They look like vanilla abandoned mineshafts, except the supports every few blocks are made of different stuff: {item:essentialcraft5:void_fence} posts, with {item:essentialcraft5:void_stone} beams and void stone patching the gaps in the floor. If you want to mine void stone directly, this is the place — a single shaft holds well over a thousand blocks. There is roughly one every two hundred and fifty blocks.

items: Some corridors have rails, and now and then a {item:minecraft:chest_minecart} carrying the usual abandoned mineshaft loot.
A corridor full of cobwebs hides a cave spider spawner. Cave spiders poison you, so have a plan for breaking the spawner before you get close.
